name: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
authors: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Beck Labash, Ashwin Gopinath, Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao (Northeastern University; MIT; Princeton University)
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (agent verbally reflects on task feedback; can use a self-as-judge LLM Evaluator or external/heuristic signals)
feedback_source: Flexible: environment-reward (scalar binary success in ALFWorld), unit-tests / self-generated test suites (code), exact-match grading (reasoning), and internally-simulated LLM self-evaluation; the trial feedback is then converted by a Self-Reflection LLM into verbal feedback
iteration_structure: episodic-retry-with-reset: the agent attempts a task over multiple trials; after each failed trial it generates a verbal self-reflection, stores it in memory, and retries the same task from a reset start with reflections appended to context
reflection_object: action trajectory and reasoning chain: the agent reflects on its full trial trajectory (actions + reasoning) and the resulting feedback to produce a verbal lesson; the reflection text is added to context (prompt/memory) to steer the next trial. Model weights are never modified.
requires_training: none (no weight updates; reinforcement is purely via natural-language feedback added to context / episodic memory)
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge plus task-dependent signals: an Evaluator (M_e) that may be an LLM-as-judge, a heuristic, exact-match grading, or self-generated unit tests; a separate Self-Reflection model (M_sr) turns the reward/feedback into verbal feedback. No trained reward model.
distillation_target: episodic-memory: verbal self-reflections are accumulated in an episodic memory buffer (mem) that conditions subsequent trials; this is the persisted artifact rather than weights
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered: reflective behavior is prompt/scaffold-engineered via an explicit Actor / Evaluator / Self-Reflection three-model decomposition and an episodic memory buffer, not an RL-emergent property of the base model
memory_type: long-term-episodic: an episodic memory buffer of self-reflective text (in addition to a short-term trajectory/scratchpad within a trial)
memory_persistence: cross-episode (cross-trial): reflections persist across trials of the SAME task to improve subsequent attempts; it is primarily intra-task across trials rather than cross-task transfer
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only with a bounded sliding window: each trial's reflection sr_t is appended to mem, but mem is capped at a maximum number of stored experiences Omega (usually 1-3) to fit the LLM context window; oldest entries fall out of the window
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level to step-level: reflection is generated at the end of a trajectory from the outcome signal, but the verbal reflection often identifies specific failing steps or planning mistakes (e.g., 'should have looked for the desklamp then the mug')
intra_task_vs_inter_task: primarily intra-task: experience is transferred across repeated trials of the same task instance via episodic memory; it is not designed for cross-task insight transfer (that is the role of successors like ExpeL/MetaReflection)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance via retry: the agent does not correct mid-trajectory; it completes a (failed) trial, reflects, and avoids the same mistake on the next reset trial (episodic retry)
task_domains: sequential decision-making (embodied/text games), QA/reasoning, and code generation (programming/tool-use)
benchmarks: ALFWorld (134 environments), HotpotQA, HumanEval (Python and Rust), MBPP (Python and Rust), and LeetcodeHardGym (new 40-problem Leetcode-hard benchmark introduced by the paper)
headline_result: 91.0% pass@1 on HumanEval (Python) with GPT-4 + Reflexion, surpassing the prior GPT-4 SOTA of 80.1%; also improves over strong baselines by 22% on ALFWorld, 20% on HotpotQA, and 11% on HumanEval
baselines: ReAct (frozen LLM agent) for decision-making/QA; Chain-of-Thought (CoT, with and without ground-truth context) for reasoning; base single-sample code generation (GPT-4) and prior code SOTA such as CodeT for programming
gains_vs_baseline: ALFWorld: ReAct + Reflexion completes 130/134 tasks vs ReAct alone (~+22% absolute success). HotpotQA: ~+20% over CoT/ReAct baselines (e.g., ReAct+GPT-3 0.30 -> Reflexion 0.55; CoT(GT)+GPT-4 0.68 -> 0.80). HumanEval (PY): 80.1% (GPT-4 base) -> 91.0% (+~11pp). HumanEval (RS): 60.0 -> 68.0. MBPP (RS): 70.9 -> 75.4. Leetcode Hard (PY): 7.5 -> 15.0. Note: MBPP (PY) slightly DECREASED (0.80 -> 0.77) due to false-positive self-generated tests.
compute_cost_profile: Higher inference cost than single-pass: requires multiple full trials per task plus extra LLM calls for the Evaluator and Self-Reflection models each trial (no training/gradient cost). Reasoning/decision agents used a memory cap of ~1-3 experiences; code experiments used max memory of 1 experience; up to ~12 trials shown for ALFWorld convergence. Exact token multipliers not tabulated in the paper.
known_limitations: It is natural-language policy optimization and can get stuck in non-optimal local minima; long-term memory is only a bounded sliding window (authors suggest vector/SQL databases as future work); for code generation, test-driven self-evaluation is fragile for non-deterministic/impure/hardware-dependent/concurrent functions, and self-generated unit tests can be wrong (false positives caused MBPP-PY to drop below baseline)
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier and sometimes env-reward: efficacy depends heavily on the quality of the feedback signal. Strongest results use grounded feedback (compiler/unit tests in code, environment success in ALFWorld); reasoning relies on exact-match grading or LLM self-evaluation, and self-evaluated signals are weaker and can mislead. Not purely intrinsic.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent: net-positive on ALFWorld, HotpotQA, HumanEval, LeetcodeHard, and Rust MBPP/HumanEval, but net-negative on MBPP-Python (0.80 -> 0.77) because erroneous self-generated tests yield false positives; gains track the reliability of the feedback source
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper predates the reasoning-model 'reasoning tax'/calibration line of analysis and does not report calibration metrics)
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (Reflexion is a self-improvement framework, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis method; it generates corrective reflections but does not produce a failure-mode taxonomy or multi-agent blame assignment)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets repeated/looping errors, hallucination, and inefficient planning in agent trajectories (e.g., reduces ALFWorld hallucination/inefficient-planning failures and the ~22% hallucination plateau of ReAct-only agents); relates to MAST modes such as error-loops and (later critiqued as susceptible to) superficial self-reflection
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes: code, demos, and datasets released, including the new LeetcodeHardGym benchmark (40 Leetcode hard problems released after the GPT-4 pre-training cutoff of Oct 8, 2022) at https://github.com/noahshinn024/reflexion
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023) as the underlying agent for decision-making/QA; Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023) for iterative self-evaluation; Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., 2022) and self-consistency for reasoning; Generative Agents (Park et al., 2023) for memory of experiences; code self-evaluation work such as CodeT (Chen et al., 2022) and AlphaCode (Li et al., 2022)
extended_by_or_inspired: Retroformer (retrospective agents with policy-gradient-optimized prompt/retrospective model), ExpeL (cross-task experiential learning / insight extraction), MetaReflection / METAREFLECTION (offline semantic memory of reflections, EMNLP 2024), Meta-Policy Reflexion (structured rule-admissible reflective memory), Multi-Agent Reflexion (MAR) and Generator-Critic-Verifier multi-agent variants, and Retrieval-Augmented Reflexion (RAR / vector episodic memory replacing the sliding window)
reasoning_model_native: no: Reflexion is an external prompt/scaffold framework applied to non-reasoning base models (GPT-3.5/GPT-4 era); it does not target o1/R1-style models with built-in reflection, though later work studies whether such scaffolds still help reasoning models
on_policy_distillation_link: Relevant as a contrast: Reflexion performs 'verbal' policy optimization that distills experience into episodic-memory text rather than on-policy distillation into weights; it is a training-free analogue motivating later on-policy-distillation / skill-optimization approaches that internalize such feedback into parameters
sample_efficiency: High relative to gradient RL (no fine-tuning samples needed): gains appear within a few trials (immediate spike between the first two trials) and converge over ~10-13 trials (e.g., ALFWorld over 12 consecutive trials); code experiments used a memory cap of a single experience
